students.name: Md Mahmudul Hasan
students.title: Graduate Research and Teaching Assistant
students.program: PhD in Electrical and Computer Engineering
students.researchSummary: Multimodal brain data analysis using EEG and structural MRI, combining feature engineering, deep learning, and fusion to build robust classification models.
researchTopics: EEG time-frequency feature extraction (DWT, WPD, STFT, FFT)
EEG scalogram-based deep learning (CWT scalograms + CNN/ViT backbones)
Structural MRI analysis (ROI/atlas features, morphometrics, PCA)
3D CNNs for MRI with multi-view/multi-crop aggregation
EEG–MRI multimodal fusion (feature-level fusion, gated fusion)

students.name: Koushik Roy
students.title: Graduate Research and Teaching Assistant
students.program: PhD in Electrical and Computer Engineering
students.researchSummary: Research on improving EEG-based emotion recognition using multi-source domain adaptation, focusing on reducing inter-subject variability through statistical alignment, adaptive source selection, and minimizing negative transfer; evaluated on multiple EEG datasets including LEMON.
researchTopics: Multi-source domain adaptation for EEG pattern recognition
Inter-subject variability handling using statistical alignment criteria
Adaptive source-domain selection to reduce negative transfer
Cross-subject generalization on large-scale EEG datasets (e.g., LEMON)
EEG preprocessing and comparative analysis across domains/models (Eye State classification)

students.name: Thomas Kidd
students.title: Graduate Research Assistant
students.researchSummary: Research focused on physics-based machine learning, deep learning, and intelligent engineering systems. His current work includes developing and optimizing convolutional neural networks for neutron/gamma pileup event classification and investigating interpretable representations learned by neural networks.
researchTopics: Convolutional neural networks and ResNet architectures
Interpretable machine learning and internal network representations
